comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body: assignment.json is pushed (531a547): experiment-repo delivers code/, data/, results/; figtab-repo delivers figures/ (both figures + generator code); paper-repo delivers report/ (report/report.md). The results you will cite will be in results/ with results/README.md explaining each number: results/stage1_peak.json (chi peak), results/stage2_crossing.json (T_c, bootstrap 95% CI, pairwise crossings), results/stage2_tau.csv (tau_int of |m| per L,T,seed + verdict), results/stage3_check.json (L=256 Binder vs crossing + verdict). Stage 1 is running now (~5 min); stages 2 and 3 follow from it (~15-25 min total compute). I keep this issue open until results/ has the stage-3 check, and will reply here with each file as it lands.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body: Stage 2 results pushed (27b5972), explained in `results/README.md`: `results/stage2_crossing.json` (Tc, bootstrap_seeds.ci95, variants, deviation_from_exact, autocorrelation summary), `results/stage2_tau.csv`, `results/stage2_binder.csv`. For the report: T_c from the Binder crossing = 2.259 with seed-bootstrap 95% interval [2.254, 2.268]; exact 2.2692 lies just above it (deviation −0.010). Autocorrelation verdict: 20,000 sweeps are ample at L=32, adequate at 64, but NOT enough at L=128 near T_c (tau_int(|m|) 500–1150 sweeps, N_eff ≈ 9–20 per run, burn-in only 2–4 tau) — the likely cause of the low crossing. Still to come in this issue: stage 3 (L=256 agreement verdict, ~10 min) and an extra long-run check (100k sweeps at L=32/64/128, ~30 min) that tests whether the stage-2 crossing is biased by the short runs. Please cite the JSON, not numbers from this comment. Issue stays open until both land.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body: Stage 3 pushed (d8505f1), `results/stage3_check.json` + README section. Verdict to report: **inconclusive** — the L=256 runs (10,000 sweeps after 2,000 burn-in, as specified) are not equilibrated, so they neither confirm nor refute the stage-2 crossing. The formal agreement test passes only because the errors are huge; the data fail every validity check (`validity_problems`: non-monotonic U, linear fit p<0.001, L=256 curve flatter than L=128, N/tau ≤ 6, tau windows unconverged; the series show ordering still in progress after burn-in). Two extra checks beyond the objective are running (~20–30 min): long L=32/64/128 runs (does the stage-2 crossing move toward 2.2692 with adequate sampling?) and an equilibrated L=256 repeat (`results/extra_long_check.json`, `results/extra_long256_check.json`). I'll close this issue when those land.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body: Long-run check pushed (3f82390), `results/extra_long_check.json` + README "Extra check" item 1. For the report: the headline T_c stays the stage-2 result specified by the objective (`stage2_crossing.json`, 2.259 [2.254, 2.268]). With 100,000 sweeps after 20,000 burn-in (N/tau >= 160 everywhere) the same estimator gives 2.261 [2.258, 2.270] (`Tc_long`, `bootstrap_seeds_ci95`), which contains the exact 2.2692. So the short L=128 runs made stage 2 noisier but did not bias it beyond its interval. Still to come here: the equilibrated L=256 rerun (100,000 sweeps after 30,000 burn-in, 4 seeds), which gives stage 3 an explicit verdict. It finishes in ~15 min. Issue stays open until then.

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body:
Final results are pushed (520cbd0); `results/README.md`, section "Checks beyond the objective", has a summary paragraph written for the report.
- T_c as the objective specifies (stage 2): 2.259, seed-bootstrap 95% interval [2.254, 2.268] (`stage2_crossing.json`). Keep reporting this as the stage-2 result.
- Stage 3 as specified (10,000 sweeps): inconclusive, the runs are not equilibrated (`stage3_check.json`).
- Stage 3 repeated with equilibrated L=256 runs (`extra_long256_verdict.json`): **disagree**. At T*=2.259, U rises with L (`U_by_L_at_stage2_Tc`); L=256 lies 6.7 sigma above L=128. L=256 crosses the smaller sizes at 2.267-2.269 (`crossings_with_256`), at the upper edge of the stage-2 interval and consistent with exact.
- Cause and best estimate (`reweighted_crossings.json`): the grid-cubic interpolation of stage 2 reads the crossing low. Reweighting the same data gives 2.262 [2.256, 2.271] (stage-2 runs) and 2.268 [2.266, 2.272] (long runs; exact 2.2692 inside, deviation -0.001). That is the study's best estimate.
- Autocorrelation verdict unchanged (`stage2_crossing.json` -> autocorrelation, README stage 2).
The README section above lists the caveats: crossing positions at L=256 are good to about +-0.003 because of the 0.015 grid, and the reweighting consistency is reported. Closing this request; reopen if a number you need is missing.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Locate the critical temperature T_c of the two-dimensional Ising model (square lattice, periodic boundaries, J = 1, no field) from simulations made with the given program `/initial-state/inputs/0/ising.py` (numpy only; `python3 ising.py --help`), and compare it with the exact value 2/ln(1+sqrt(2)) = 2.2692.

The study has three stages; each is designed from the result of the one before:

1. Pilot: L = 64, T from 1.5 to 3.5 in steps of 0.1, seeds 1 and 2, 20,000 measured sweeps after 2,000 burn-in. Locate the peak of the susceptibility.
2. Crossing: L = 32, 64 and 128 at 9 equally spaced temperatures from 0.12 below to 0.12 above the pilot's peak, seeds 1 to 3, 20,000 sweeps, keeping the time series (`--series`). Estimate T_c where the Binder cumulants of the three sizes cross, with a bootstrap 95% interval over seeds, and the integrated autocorrelation time of |m| at each point, to say whether 20,000 sweeps are enough.
3. Check: L = 256 at 5 equally spaced temperatures from 0.03 below to 0.03 above the stage-2 estimate, seeds 1 and 2, 10,000 sweeps. Say whether the L = 256 Binder values agree with the stage-2 crossing.

Deliver the data and analysis code of every stage, two figures (the pilot's susceptibility and heat capacity against T; the Binder cumulants of all sizes near the crossing), and a one-page report `report/report.md` (Markdown is enough) with T_c, its interval, the comparison with the exact value and what stage 3 showed. On this machine a single stage takes several minutes or more.
